_comment: THE JOURNEY LEDGER (#927). ONE ledger, keyed `surface / journey / volume / hardware`. It replaces tests/experience-budgets/{web,desktop,mobile,gateway,client-query-counts}.json, tests/budgets.json#qualityRigs and tests/budgets.json#experience: a ceiling stated without the volume and the hardware it was measured on is not a budget, and four files keyed by surface alone could not say so. Every entry names the SPANS it is measured from (packages/core/src/protocol/trace.ts) and the CONSUMERS that assert it, so a ceiling with no reader and a reader with no ceiling are both visible here. Read through tests/helpers/journeys.ts (TypeScript) or scripts/lib/journey-ledger.mjs (scripts); nothing parses this file by hand. Ratcheted tighten-only as a PERF_BUDGET_SOURCE (scripts/test-report/ratchet-floors.mjs): `max*`/`ceiling*` fall freely and widening one needs an `approvedDeviation`; `min*` may only rise. A leading underscore is invisible to the ratchet, which is how an intended-but-unobserved ceiling is parked without gating vacuously. RE-KEYING an entry (a journey measured at a new volume, say) renames its flattened numbers, which the ratchet reads as a removal plus an addition — i.e. a widen: carry the same numbers across and add an `approvedDeviation` saying what moved and why.

_statusVocabulary.measured: A real run on the stated date and hardware produced `_provenance.observed*`; the ceiling is that value plus the stated headroom.
_statusVocabulary.projected: Arithmetic on a measured number from a different volume or surface. `_basis` names what it extrapolates from. Never presented as observed.
_statusVocabulary.unmeasured: NO NUMBER. The ceiling key is absent and nothing gates. `probe` names the rig that will fill it.
_statusVocabulary._intended: A ceiling that is known but not yet observable on this hardware, parked under a leading underscore so it documents intent without gating.
_statusVocabulary.bound: A CATASTROPHE BOUND, not observed+headroom: a value above which the experience is broken on any hardware and needs no measurement to assert. It gates, but it is not a measurement, and the real target is parked beside it under a leading underscore until a run produces a distribution. `_provenance.note` must argue the bound.

hardware.dev-darwin-arm64: Apple-silicon development host, NVMe. Faster than any CI runner; a ceiling seeded here carries extra headroom and says so.
hardware.ci-ios-sim: iOS simulator on a macOS runner, release-configuration build with the Hermes bundle embedded.
hardware.ci-android-emu: Android emulator on a linux runner, release-configuration build.
hardware.any: Hardware-independent — a build artifact weighed on disk, or a count of statements the product issues.
hardware.ci-linux-x64-4c-standard: The same runner as `ci-linux-x64-4c`, with CENTRAID_HARDWARE_PROFILE=standard pinned: SQLite `synchronous=FULL`, the desktop-class durability setting. The gateway resolves the profile at boot, so a number is only comparable to another taken under the SAME profile.
hardware.ci-linux-x64-4c-constrained: The same runner with CENTRAID_HARDWARE_PROFILE=constrained: SQLite `synchronous=NORMAL`, the phone/low-end setting. Every gateway journey is stated under BOTH profiles because the durability mode is the single biggest lever on a write path and one number would hide which side of it moved.

volumes.year3: The golden year-3 artifact: ~27,600 domain rows (5,000 parties, 10,000 photos, 200 conversations x 12 turns, 1,000 notes, 1,096 events, 12 grantees, 365 receipt days). packages/test-kit/src/year3-vault.ts.

volumes.year3-household: 5 mounted vaults = 10 SQLite handles on one gateway.
volumes.year3-10gib: 10 GiB of CAS bytes across 4 MiB objects + 95,640 FK-checked rows.
volumes.empty: A FRESH VAULT. A bundle or transport ratchet only: it cannot catch an O(vault-size) regression, and an entry that stays here is an admission, not a budget.
volumes.build-artifact: Bytes on disk after a build; independent of vault size.
volumes.seeded-demo: Every bundled app's own demo seed written through the gateway's write path, plus a stated number of Atlas `core.place` rows (the count is in each entry's provenance). NOT year-3: reaching the declared 10,000-photo daily path from an e2e harness needs the kit's year-3 generator, and `@centraid/test-kit` ships TypeScript sources with no build, which `node --experimental-strip-types` cannot load. It is a real volume through the real write path, and it is the volume the number below is stated at.
volumes.mock-gateway: The desktop e2e fixture: a mock gateway, one app, a fresh userData directory. NOT year-3, and the harness cannot be pointed at the golden artifact from this container — Electron does not launch on a display-less runner, so the rig is landed and the number stays parked.
volumes.device-fixture: Whatever the CI gateway fixture seeded onto the simulator's device replica. NOT the declared year-3 50,000 replica rows / 90,000 photo assets: reaching those needs a device run, which this container has none of.
volumes.shared-album: One album of 200 photos, shared whole. Big enough that projection dominates the grant plane's fixed cost.

journeys.core-route: Not a journey — the per-route p95 of the gateway's own core routes.
journeys.restore: Not a journey — backup restore wall clock.
journeys.integrity-check: Not a journey — post-restore FK/integrity verification.

_provenance.host: linux x64 worktree, `bun run --cwd apps/web build` (vite build + precompress)
_provenance.note: MEASURED by `node scripts/perf/app-weight.mjs --surface web --report` (#781, closing the #587 D21 web gap; re-measured and TIGHTENED by #883 C5). The earlier 'a weigh-in here would be a duplicate owner' claim was wrong: perf-budgets.ts shell.maxTransferBytes fences what the BROWSER transfers on the e2e shell journey (compressed, journey-scoped), not what the build ships on disk — the two can diverge by megabytes without either gate noticing the other's regression. Source maps plus the .br/.gz precompress sidecars (17.6 MB together) are excluded as diagnostics/alternate encodings of already-weighed bytes. THE DOUBLE-SHIPPED IROH WASM IS FIXED: the 1,995,618 B binding had two inclusion paths — the page's wasm-bindgen ESM resolving new URL('centraid_web_iroh_bg.wasm', import.meta.url) into a hashed assets/ copy, and scripts/build-iroh-worker.mjs copying the same bytes to public/centraid-worker-iroh.wasm for the CLASSIC service worker, which cannot import ESM. The worker's copy has to keep its unhashed, _headers-pinned path, so the centraid-iroh-wasm-single-copy plugin in apps/web/vite.config.ts rewrites the bindings' default to that same ?v=-stamped URL and the assets/ copy stops being emitted; public/sw.js now treats that path as an immutable shell entry, so a visit that uses both the page transport and the worker pays the 2 MB once. Measured on this host the same day: 10,074,585 B across 87 files before, 8,083,152 B across 86 files after. maxTotalBytes ratcheted 11,010,048 -> 8,730,000 (observed + ~8%). maxLargestChunkBytes is UNCHANGED at 2,200,000 deliberately: the largest single file is still that same 1,995,618 B binary — de-duplication removed a COPY, not weight from the copy that remains — so the existing observed+10% ceiling is still the honest one, and tightening it here would claim a win that did not happen. Next largest: pdf.worker.min.mjs 1.30 MB, boot.js 1.10 MB, sqlite3.wasm 865 kB; pdf.worker is the next real cut.
_provenance.headroom: observed + ~8% total; largest chunk + ~10% (mirrors the desktop/mobile seeds)

sendToFirstToken.probe: RIG EXISTS, NO NUMBER YET — and the distinction is the point. The blocker named here until #890 was that the CI gateway had no model provider at all, so no turn could start and nothing could be timed. That is fixed: tests/agent-e2e-mobile/lib/fixed-delay-agent.mjs is a minimal ACP agent that streams its first token after a KNOWN delay, tests/agent-e2e-mobile/lib/ci-gateway.mjs configures it as the Assistant's provider through the registry's `acp` custom-agent kind, and tests/integration-mobile/assistant-provider.integration.test.ts proves that wiring resolves to a launch plan spawning it (importing the prefs the gateway writes rather than a copy, so the two cannot drift). What is still missing is a DEVICE RUN: the flow that taps send and waits for first paint, on hardware this change had none of. Until that runs, `status` stays `unmeasured` — a rig is not a measurement, and promoting this to `measured` on the strength of wiring is the exact move this budget file exists to prevent. When the flow lands, the number to record is `observed − CENTRAID_STUB_FIRST_TOKEN_DELAY_MS` (default 250), which is the dead time this repo owns: the app's send path, the Iroh hop, gateway turn dispatch and the renderer reaching first paint. The gateway-side lower bound on the same interval is already measured in tests/experience-budgets/gateway.json (#842) and excludes every one of those spans.

reconnectToFresh.probe: node node_modules/vitest/vitest.mjs run --config vitest.scale.config.ts tests/scale/mobile-reconnect-to-fresh.scale.test.ts (also `bun run test:scale`) — the nightly scale lane rather than the package suite, because this gates on WALL CLOCK and `bun run test` drives 29 turbo tasks across four threads: under that contention the probe read 3,292 ms against this 1,800 ms ceiling while reading 482 ms alone, so the lane's `fileParallelism: false` forked pool is what makes the number mean anything. It drives the production createNativeReplicaSession: bootstrap, AppState 'background' (feed deactivated), server state advances unseen, AppState 'active', then polls the read a Photos/Docs screen issues until every missed change is on the page. The clock starts on the AppState transition and stops when the SCREEN'S read is fresh, not when the delta lands in SQLite.

_provenance.host: linux x64 development container, Node SQLite driver under the production native session
_provenance.note: RE-MEASURED AFTER PUSHDOWN (#883 C3/D1) and tightened from 20,000 ms. The previous entry measured 6,324-8,382 ms and said in as many words that the screen read was the shrinker: every read materialised all 50,000 rows, JSON.parsed each payload and filtered/sorted in JavaScript before the 200-row limit applied. The compiled read plan made that read one SQL statement, and the same probe now resumes to a fresh screen in ~0.5 s — a 15x fall with no change to what is measured. Scope is UNCHANGED and this ceiling must not be read as the whole interval. INCLUDED: the AppState transition, change-feed reactivation, the delta pull loop, applying 200 missed changes, and the 200-row newest-first screen read that has to return them. EXCLUDED: real network RTT (the gateway is an in-process fetch double - the gateway's side of the same interval is measured over real HTTP at 60 ms by tests/scale/replica-reconnect.scale.test.ts, see gateway.json), device flash I/O (node:sqlite in memory here, op-sqlite on flash there), and React render. So this is still a LOWER BOUND on what the owner feels. The ceiling is ~3.2x the slowest of four samples because a shared CI runner is materially slower than this host and four samples cannot bound its jitter; TIGHTEN further once ~10 nightly samples exist.

_provenance.note: MEASURED, and what it replaces is NO NUMBER AT ALL — before this rig every perf/scale rig in the repo measured one dimension against an otherwise idle gateway. The headline is reassuring: running the whole household together costs about the same WALL CLOCK as running the lanes one after another (0.75-1.05x), so the gateway is genuinely overlapping work rather than serializing behind one lock. THE FINDING THAT IS NOT reassuring is the per-lane spread: the cheapest lane (Atlas ref-search, ~5 ms solo) degrades 27-66x under composition, to 217-361 ms. That is the app-engine worker spawns (create-note and search each spawn a capped worker thread, and this host admits only 2 at once) taking the CPU away from an in-gateway read. It is a fairness observation, not a refusal or a correctness failure — every op completed and nothing was shed. Per-lane latency ratios are therefore PUBLISHED BY THE RIG BUT NOT GATED: a ratio over a ~5 ms denominator fences scheduler noise, and a gate that flakes is a gate that gets widened.

_provenance.runs: one 10-minute run (483 cycles, 7,245 ops) plus one 0.75-minute run (41 cycles, 615 ops)
_provenance.note: MEASURED, and the shape matters more than any single number. RSS slope is 20.4 kB/cycle over 10 minutes against 1.19 MB/cycle over 45 seconds — a 58x DROP as the run lengthens, which is what warm-up amortizing looks like and NOT what a leak looks like; a leak's per-cycle slope is flat or rising. heapUsed and arrayBuffers both trend NEGATIVE over the long run (GC reclaiming), and open descriptors are bounded (peak 83, spread 24) across 7,245 ops. TWO HONEST CAVEATS. (1) declaredSoakMinutes is 10 because ten minutes is the longest run these ceilings were actually derived from — a genuine multi-day soak has never been executed (see the blocked-external note on #842 W3.4); the weekly lane's multi-hour setting is what turns these into a real distribution.
